label: early copy phase (2nd-3rd outputs) of long sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost entirely at the steps that output original tokens 1 and 2 (recall_idx 2 holds 70% of mass, recall_idx 1 holds 27%, recall_idx 3 a little). It never fires in the original phase, at the delimiter, at recall_idx 0, or at recall_idx >= 4. Rate and mass go up with sequence length: L=9 carries 52% of mass, L<=5 almost none. Within that window it is sparse and depends on tokens. It is strongest when the early original tokens (orig(1)/orig(2), seen as in_tok or out_tok) are f, a, r, p, q, j or o. The top activations are mostly at recall_idx 2 with input f, i.e. sequences like ? f a r .... Even orig(1)==f gives only about 34% precision, so a hidden-state factor not captured here gates firing. Positional predicate: mass recall about 0.91, precision about 0.08. Adding the token set raises precision to about 0.14 with mass recall 0.84.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: f, a, l, p, q, c; least: 0, t, h, m) and the token being output (most: f, a, r, p, j, o; least: h, -, w, v); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=2, recall_idx=1, t=10.
